claim: SR stores discounted expected future visits under a given policy, M=(I-gamma P)^-1, and can be learned by TD; it supports fast reward revaluation but is tied to the policy that generated it.
agent_test: Store per-class 'where this leads' counts (next-step class frequencies, discounted) from past runs; re-derive when the operator mix changes. Compare with no memory at equal tokens.
audit_note: Dayan 1993 formula did not extract as text from the PDF; SR definition, TD learning, latent learning and policy-dependence/staleness confirmed via Dayan's text and Russek et al. 2017.

claim: Humans show both MF and MB signatures on the two-step task (reward main effect plus reward x transition interaction, N=17 in the original). Re-opened 2026-10-31: N=17, 201 trials, interaction p<5e-5, median MF weight 61% (d01).
agent_test: Run the stay-probability regression on agent traces (repeat choice after rewarded rare vs common transition) to label the agent's control mode.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Human revaluation is asymmetric: reward changes are adapted to better than transition changes (0.52 vs 0.45, N=58; replicated N=88). Pure MB and pure MF both fail to predict this; SR-like or hybrid SR+MB fits better. Re-opened 2026-10-31: Exp 1 N=58 (69 recruited, 11 excluded), reward vs transition t(57)=2.89 p<.01; Exp 2 N=88 (115 recruited, 27 excluded). The 0.52 vs 0.45 pair is in figures and is still unchecked (d02, d03).
agent_test: Test the agent on reward-change vs transition-change revaluation in a text graph at equal tokens; see whether an SR-style cache shows the same asymmetry.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: The asymmetry has a rival account (Kalman-filter TD SR with non-local updates), so it is not unique evidence for an SR in the brain.
agent_test: Not testable on the agent; treat SR as an engineering option, not a proven brain mechanism.

claim: Policy revaluation (a changed distal reward that flips the best earlier action) is hard for humans and for SR without replay; Dyna-style replay repairs it.
agent_test: On a graph task change a distal reward; compare agent with and without a replay/re-plan step over stored episodes at equal tokens.
audit_note: Both the human result (Momennejad et al. 2017, N=88, policy resembles transition revaluation and differs from reward revaluation, p=.0043 / .5771) and the simulation (Russek et al. 2017) come from the same research group (Momennejad, Russek, Botvinick, Daw, Gershman are on both); the Dyna repair is simulation-only, and b03's cited 'Carvalho 2024 review' URL is actually the Momennejad paper.

claim: The standard two-step task gives MB control almost no payoff; a redesigned task where MB pays off raises MB use and ties MB weight to reward rate (r=0.55 vs 0.10).
agent_test: Test a payoff-aware gate for deliberate planning against always-plan at equal tokens.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Two-step task signatures are ambiguous in both directions: model-free strategies can mimic model-based behaviour (Akam et al. 2015, simulations), and pure model-based agents with a wrong task model are labelled hybrid (median w 0.36 or 0.80 vs 0.94 for a correct model); with a detailed story and comprehension checks, humans in one study (Feher da Silva & Hare 2020, N=21 and N=24) were mostly model-based (median w 0.78-0.79).
agent_test: When measuring the agent's MF/MB mix, check prompt ambiguity first; run the same task with clear and unclear instructions.
audit_note: Akam et al. 2015 show model-free strategies can look model-based (the opposite artefact: false MB signatures), so they do not support 'apparent model-free influence is an artefact'; only Feher da Silva & Hare 2020 supports the false-hybrid / mostly-MB claim, and it is one lab's single study (spaceship N=21, magic carpet N=24).
claim_before_audit: Apparent model-free influence in the two-step task is partly an artefact: MF strategies can mimic MB (Akam), and misunderstood instructions make pure MB agents look hybrid; with better instructions humans are mostly MB.

claim: Reduced MB control tracks compulsivity, not depression or anxiety, in large online samples (N=548 beta -0.040 p=.049; N=1413 beta -0.026 p=.020).
agent_test: Not relevant to the agent; kept as boundary evidence.

claim: Right dlPFC theta-burst stimulation reduces MB control (N=25, p=.01).
agent_test: None.

claim: Two-step RL parameters have poor test-retest reliability (ICC .02-.52 for bandit parameters).
agent_test: Repeat the same item many times and report variance before reading a mode into one run.

claim: Offline replay during rest predicts later replanning after a reward change (N=24, rho=0.54), triggered by surprise.
agent_test: Add an offline replay of surprising episodes between attempts; compare with none at equal tokens.

claim: SR eigenvectors resemble grid fields and find bottleneck subgoals; hippocampal place fields fit SR rows qualitatively.
agent_test: Use bottleneck states of the agent's own state graph as subgoal candidates; compare with random subgoals.

claim: Successor features plus generalized policy improvement transfer old policies to new reward weights with guarantees in RL.
agent_test: Cache solution strategies by task class; on a new goal pick the cached strategy that scores best, then refine. Test against a fresh start.
audit: downgraded 2026-10-31 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Humans reuse a previously good policy on a new reward even when suboptimal, and humans and rats on a maze behave most like SR agents.
agent_test: Check whether the agent over-reuses cached strategies on changed goals; add a mismatch check.

claim: GPT-3 shows an MB-like stay pattern on the two-step task (200 simulations), though it fails causal reasoning and is prompt-sensitive.
agent_test: Replicate with current models using the same prompt plus a prompt-perturbation set.

claim: LLM model-basedness on the two-step task rises with size (beta=0.481), chain-of-thought (+64.59%) and step-back (+118.59%); code tuning does not help.
agent_test: Add step-back and CoT arms to the two-step prompt and to planning items at equal tokens.

claim: LLMs plan poorly on cognitive-map revaluation tasks: GPT-4 0.99 on 1-step but 0.47 on n-step path and 0.21 on policy revaluation; 0/30 on shortest path one cluster away; BFS/DFS prompts help little. Paired view from CogEval Table 3: reward and transition revaluation are within noise for GPT-4 (0.67 vs 0.60, SD ~0.4); the large gap is policy revaluation (d04).
agent_test: Rerun CogEval items with the scaffold (explicit graph state, monitor of invalid edges) vs plain at equal tokens.

claim: Modular planning (monitor rejecting invalid moves, state predictor, evaluator, decomposer) raises solve rates and removes invalid moves; removing the monitor gives 31% invalid moves.
agent_test: Ablate a validity-monitor guardrail in the scaffold; measure invalid-step rate and solves at equal tokens.

claim: Using an LLM as a world model to simulate outcomes (MCTS in RAP; one-step imagination in WebDreamer) beats reactive or CoT baselines: RAP Blocksworld 6-step 0.26-0.42 vs CoT 0.00 (LLaMA-33B); WebDreamer 23.6 vs reactive 17.6 on VisualWebArena.
agent_test: Compare reactive, one-step imagination and tree search at equal tokens; imagination is the cheap middle way.
audit_note: RAP's 6-step LLaMA-33B result (0.26-0.42) is still at or below GPT-4 CoT (0.40) at the low setting; WebDreamer 23.6 is below tree search (26.2); claim compares to the stated baselines only.

claim: Imagination-then-commit costs far less than real-interaction tree search (about 3x fewer steps, 10x lower latency, 4-5x more efficient) but stays below tree search on VisualWebArena (23.6 vs 26.2).
agent_test: Budget-matched comparison of imagination vs search.

claim: Llama 70B represents in-context graph structure more like the SR than the transition matrix (max r 0.62 vs 0.49); a TD-error latent exists (r 0.60) and lesioning it lowers accuracy; 8B stays at chance.
agent_test: Probe whether an explicit class-transition table helps more than a raw trace; the 70B result suggests the model builds this itself only at scale.

claim: Transformers can implement TD learning in the forward pass (proved for linear attention), and meta-trained transformers form predictive-map-like representations and find shortcuts in over 60% of tests.
agent_test: Background; no direct agent test.
audit_note: Predictive-map-like is the authors' 'resembles predictive representation learning' qualitative claim, not a tested equivalence.

claim: Training regime shapes the planning algorithm: random-walk training gives a map-like code, shortest-path training gives brittle heuristics (0% off-length).
agent_test: Background; not an in-context test.

claim: Parametric learners fail to use information not needed at training (reversal curse, latent learning); episodic retrieval fixes much of this, only if training has in-context-learning sequences.
agent_test: Test retrieval of stored past episodes for a new goal vs none at equal tokens.

claim: Fine-tuned Centaur reproduces two-step behaviour (NLL 0.4998), but retrieval-augmented agents given the reward structure matched its likelihood, so good fit may not imply human-like process.
agent_test: Do not infer cognition from choice-likelihood fit when evaluating the agent.

claim: An SR of an LLM-agent communication graph predicts topology failure: condition number rs=1.0, spectral radius rs=-1.0 (inverted), Qwen2.5-7B, 100 trials.
agent_test: Only 3 topologies, so rank correlations are near-degenerate; not a design rule.

claim: A TD-valued action-graph memory for LLM agents (GAMER) beats other memory baselines: 31.60 vs 26.31 vanilla; Reflexion 20.81.
agent_test: Closest existing MF-in-memory design; replicate suggestion/avoidance values at equal tokens.

claim: No LLM-agent memory built directly on successor representations was found in about 12 queries (as of 2026-10-31). Second search 2026-10-31 (about 30 arXiv queries) again found none (d16).
agent_test: If true, an SR-style class-transition memory is untested; build and test.

claim: Successor eigenvectors give intrinsic-reward options, and deep SRs adapt faster to distal reward change.
agent_test: Background.

claim: Human reward-vs-transition asymmetry is not reproduced as a consistent pattern in LLMs on CogEval: reward minus transition revaluation is +0.07 (GPT-4), -0.02 (GPT-3.5), -0.15 (davinci), -0.07 (Claude-1) with SDs near 0.4; no paired test exists.
agent_test: Run the Momennejad design on current models with a paired test before assuming a human-like asymmetry.

claim: Daw 2011 and Momennejad 2017 primary numbers confirmed from full text: Daw N=17, interaction p<5e-5, median MF weight 61%; Momennejad Exp 1 N=58 (11 of 69 excluded), t(57)=2.89; Exp 2 N=88 (27 of 115 excluded, a 23% exclusion).
agent_test: Cite exclusions with the effect; the asymmetry is modest and rests on one lab's two samples.

claim: In a training-free LLM web agent, a structured cognitive-map memory beat both no memory and raw-trace memory: WebArena-Lite 57.4 vs 47.9 base vs 44.8 raw (Claude-4-Sonnet, one run each, tokens not matched); full stack with look-ahead simulation 63.0.
agent_test: Closest evidence for structured over raw memory; still needs an equal-token, multi-seed test on our benchmarks.

claim: A procedure graph of stage transitions with reliability scores, used as soft guidance, beat Reflexion (37.4 vs 32.2) and ExpeL (36.3) on ScienceWorld; removing the graph costs 2.6 points and forcing the plan costs 4.8.
agent_test: Use class-transition memory as advice the agent may override, not as a rule.

claim: Cost gates for thinking can cut tokens without losing accuracy: AdaptThink (trained) -44.7% to -63.5% length with +1.4 to +4.1 points on a 1.5B model; DART (training-free, draft agreement) -32% to -73% thinking tokens with gains up to +9.0 (math) and +22.5 (code) points.
agent_test: Try a draft-agreement gate before expensive planning; none of these prices payoffs as Kool 2016 does, so the payoff-aware version remains untested.

claim: Replay of failed attempts helps LLM agents in two forms: in-context hindsight relabelling (ECHO beats Reflexion and AWM in XMiniGrid, but gains are mixed across organisations) and fine-tuning with prioritised replay (PPER). No study replays by surprise in a frozen-model loop.
agent_test: Test surprise-ranked retry notes against recency-ranked notes at equal tokens.

claim: World-model simulation inside the reasoning can match a much larger model at half the tokens (Dyna-Think 32B vs R1 685B, best-of-n, 2x fewer tokens) but this was trained, and no prompt-only matched-budget comparison of one-step imagination vs tree search vs CoT on current models was found.
agent_test: Keep the matched-budget comparison as an open test.

claim: No measured test was found (searched 2026-10-31) of: frontier-model CogEval revaluation, scaffolded graph-state closing the policyReval gap, SR-memory failure under policy change, Kalman-TD SR on human data, or test-retest reliability of an LLM MF/MB index.
agent_test: Treat gaps 2, 4, 7, 10 as open; the LLM bandit fits (d15) show rigidity, not reliability.
